boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Creighton University
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night food and supply runs for Creighton University students, featuring on-campus dining and local Omaha favorites open late.

cards.title: The Skutt Convenience Hub
cards.subtitle: Skutt Student Center
cards.notes: Grab snacks, toiletries, or a quick pizza at this on-campus market. It serves as a primary late-night resource for students in the Skutt Student Center.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus convenience store in the Skutt Student Center offering snacks and essentials until 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Jack and Ed's Marketplace is open until 10 p.m. Monday through Thursday and on Sundays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 p.m. Mon-Thu and Sun; closes at 7 p.m. Fri-Sat.

cards.title: Late-Night Dining at Skutt
cards.subtitle: Skutt Student Center
cards.notes: Visit the Skutt Student Center for a late-night meal. This retail dining area offers options like Qdoba and Firehouse Subs during designated late hours.
cards.short_summary: A retail dining hub on campus offering late-night food options for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Wareham Court offers late-night dining hours from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours are 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Monday through Thursday.

cards.title: Finals Week Late Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Brandeis Building
cards.notes: Join the tradition of Late Night Breakfast during finals week. Faculty and staff serve breakfast foods to students to fuel their late-night study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A signature Creighton tradition where students gather for a late-night meal served by faculty during finals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Late Night Breakfast event at Brandeis Dining Hall runs from 10 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. during finals week.
cards.access_notes: Event typically occurs from 10 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. on the Monday of finals week.

cards.title: The Blackstone Cookie Run
cards.subtitle: Blackstone District
cards.notes: Head to the Blackstone District for warm cookies and ice cream. It is a popular late-night destination for students seeking a sweet treat after dark.
cards.short_summary: A late-night bakery in the Blackstone District serving warm cookies until 1 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: The Insomnia Cookies location in the Blackstone District is open until 1 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Open until 1 a.m. daily for pickup and delivery.

cards.title: 24-Hour Taco Stop
cards.subtitle: 44th and Dodge
cards.notes: Drive through for authentic Mexican food at any hour. This spot is a staple for students needing a substantial meal in the middle of the night.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour Mexican restaurant with a drive-thru located near campus on Dodge Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Abelardo's Mexican Fresh drive-thru is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is open 24/7.

cards.title: The Late-Night Chicken Run
cards.subtitle: 70th and Dodge
cards.notes: Drive out to Dodge Street for a Box Combo. This location stays open much later than others, making it a prime target for late-night cravings.
cards.short_summary: A popular chicken finger restaurant on Dodge Street open until 2 a.m. on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: The Raising Cane's on Dodge Street is open until 2 a.m. on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's in Omaha, NE - 7060 Dodge Street
cards.access_notes: Open until 2 a.m. Thu-Sat; until 12 a.m. Sun-Wed.

cards.title: Midtown Sandwich Stop
cards.subtitle: Farnam Midtown
cards.notes: Order a toasted sandwich or pizza in Midtown. It's a convenient stop for students in the Blackstone or Midtown area during late study nights.
cards.short_summary: A gourmet cafe in Midtown Omaha serving toasted sandwiches and pizza until 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickleman's Gourmet Cafe in Farnam Midtown is open until 10 p.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 p.m. every day.

cards.title: The Turner Park Supply Run
cards.subtitle: 30th and Dodge
cards.notes: Pick up snacks, beverages, or health essentials near campus. This location is a reliable late-night resource for students living in nearby residence halls.
cards.short_summary: A pharmacy and convenience store near campus open until 11 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walgreens at 3001 Dodge St is open until 11 p.m. every day.
cards.source_title: 3001 DODGE ST, Omaha, NE 68131 - Walgreens Pharmacy
cards.access_notes: Store and photo department open until 11 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Dodge Street Essentials
cards.subtitle: 48th and Dodge
cards.notes: Stop by for late-night groceries or pharmacy needs. Located along the ORBT line, it's easily accessible for students without cars.
cards.short_summary: A pharmacy and retail store on Dodge Street providing late-night access to essentials.
cards.evidence_claim: The CVS Pharmacy at 4840 Dodge St is open until 11 p.m. on Mondays and Saturdays.
cards.source_title: CVS Pharmacy at 4840 Dodge St. Omaha, NE 68132
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 p.m. Mon and Sat; until 9 p.m. Tue-Fri; until 10 p.m. Sun.

cards.title: The Study Fuel Station
cards.subtitle: Skutt Student Center
cards.notes: Get a caffeine boost for late-night studying. This on-campus Starbucks is a central meeting point for students working in the student center.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus Starbucks location in the Skutt Student Center open until 7 p.m. on weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: The Skutt Student Center Starbucks is open until 7 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 7 p.m. Mon-Thu; closes earlier on weekends.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, quiet reflection spaces, and student-centric hubs that define daily life at Creighton University beyond the standard tour route.

cards.title: Reservable Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Quiet zones for focused academic work
cards.notes: Book these 1-2 person rooms online for up to two hours to ensure a private, distraction-free environment for deep study or remote exams.
cards.short_summary: Private, reservable rooms in the main library designed for individual or pair study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reinert-Alumni Library offers reservable 1-2 person study rooms to help students concentrate, bookable through an online system.
cards.access_notes: Available during library operating hours; requires Creighton ID for reservation and access.

cards.title: Fireplace Lounge
cards.subtitle: The campus living room
cards.notes: Located on the ground level near Starbucks, this cozy spot is ideal for casual reading or meeting friends between classes.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable lounge area featuring a central fireplace and proximity to on-campus coffee.
cards.evidence_claim: The Skutt Student Center is known as the 'living room of the campus' and features a cozy central fireplace lounge for study and relaxation.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; late-night access typically follows student center hours (often until 11 PM or midnight).

cards.title: Mutual of Omaha (MOO) Lounge
cards.subtitle: Second-floor science hub
cards.notes: Visit the second floor to find this popular lounge where science students gather to study, snack, and collaborate between labs.
cards.short_summary: A bustling student lounge located within the Hixson-Lied Science Building atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hixson-Lied Science Building houses the popular Mutual of Omaha (MOO) Lounge on the second floor for student study and connection.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours; primarily used by students in science programs.

cards.title: Harper Center Huddle Rooms
cards.subtitle: Collaborative business spaces
cards.notes: Utilize these small group rooms for team projects or interview prep; they are scattered throughout the Heider College of Business floors.
cards.short_summary: Small, glass-walled rooms designed for group collaboration and professional preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harper Center, home to the Heider College of Business, features huddle rooms and lounge spaces for student study.
cards.source_title: Mike and Josie Harper Center - Creighton University
cards.access_notes: Open during Harper Center hours; priority often given to business students for specific rooms.

cards.title: Taizé Prayer Services
cards.subtitle: Evening meditative worship
cards.notes: Attend these candlelit, ecumenical services for a quiet hour of mantra songs and silence to decompress from academic stress.
cards.short_summary: A meditative evening prayer service held in the historic campus church.
cards.evidence_claim: St. John's Church hosts Prayer in the Style of Taizé, a meditative evening prayer with music, throughout the academic year.
cards.source_title: Worship, Prayer and Sacraments on Campus - Creighton University
cards.access_notes: Held on specific evenings during the academic year; open to all students regardless of faith background.

cards.title: eGaming Suite
cards.subtitle: Campus esports and gaming hub
cards.notes: Head to the KFC to find this dedicated space for competitive and casual gaming, featuring high-end PCs and console setups.
cards.short_summary: A modern gaming facility for student recreation and official esports team practice.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kiewit Fitness Center includes an eGaming Suite where students can play during open recreation hours or join esports teams.
cards.access_notes: Open during KFC hours: Mon-Thu until 11 PM, Fri-Sat until 10 PM, Sun until 11 PM.

cards.title: Creighton Hall Patio Rocking Chairs
cards.subtitle: Historic outdoor relaxation
cards.notes: Take a break in the signature rocking chairs on the patio of the university's oldest building for a view of the central campus mall.
cards.short_summary: A popular outdoor seating area featuring rocking chairs outside the historic main administration building.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can be found outside Creighton Hall on the patio in the popular rocking chairs.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible 24/7; chairs are typically available during warmer months.

cards.title: Success Hub
cards.subtitle: Residential academic support
cards.notes: Open to all students, these hubs provide a dedicated environment for peer tutoring and focused study within the residence halls.
cards.short_summary: Academic support spaces located within first-year residence halls, open to the entire student body.
cards.evidence_claim: All first-year residence halls, including Graves Hall, include a Success Hub dedicated to personal academic support and study, open to all students.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to residents; non-residents may need to be swiped in or visit during specific hub hours.

cards.title: Indoor Fieldhouse Turf
cards.subtitle: Multi-sport recreational field
cards.notes: Check the internal schedule for open turf hours to play soccer, frisbee, or participate in intramural sports on the 60x40 yard field.
cards.short_summary: A large indoor synthetic turf field used for intramurals and open student recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rasmussen Center features a 60- x 40-yard turf fieldhouse available for student use at no charge.
cards.access_notes: Open turf hours are posted internally; closed during university breaks and summer.

cards.title: St. Peter Faber Chapel
cards.subtitle: Quiet reflection in Harper
cards.notes: Find this quiet sanctuary on the main floor of the Harper Center for a moment of silence or to attend Protestant/Christian worship services.
cards.short_summary: A modern chapel located within the Harper Center providing a space for prayer and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harper Center houses the St. Peter Faber, SJ, Chapel on the main floor, offering a place for reflection and Protestant worship.
cards.access_notes: Open during Harper Center hours; Protestant/Christian worship held Sundays at 8 PM during the academic year.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Creighton University, from quiet gardens to creative tech labs.

cards.title: Relax in the Jesuit Gardens
cards.subtitle: Historic green space behind St. John's Church
cards.notes: Walk through these manicured gardens for a quiet outdoor break. It is a popular spot for photos and peaceful reflection near the heart of campus.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus quadrangle featuring walking paths and green space behind St. John's Church.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jesuit Gardens are described as a picturesque destination for social gatherings and a historic heart of the campus with no admission fee.
cards.source_title: Conferences and Event Services | Creighton University
cards.access_notes: Open daily to the public and campus community; accessible via the main campus mall.

cards.title: Browse the Lied Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Fine arts exhibitions in the Lied Education Center
cards.notes: View rotating exhibitions of student and professional art. The gallery is free and open to the public during the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery hosting up to eight exhibitions annually featuring local and international artists.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Lied Art Gallery is free and open to the public when exhibitions are present.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-8 p.m. and weekends 10 a.m.-4 p.m. during exhibitions.

cards.title: Hang Out in the Skutt Center
cards.subtitle: The 'Living Room' of campus
cards.notes: Relax by the central fireplace or meet friends in the lounge. This hub offers plenty of seating for socializing without needing to buy anything.
cards.short_summary: The primary student union on campus featuring lounges, meeting rooms, and social spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Skutt Student Center is referred to as the 'living room of campus' and is a place for socializing and relaxing.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; typically closes at 11 p.m. on weeknights.

cards.title: Visit the Billy Bluejay Statue
cards.subtitle: Iconic mascot bronze at Morrison Stadium
cards.notes: Stop by Morrison Stadium to see the 6-foot bronze mascot. It's a campus tradition to tap the bird's beak for good luck.
cards.short_summary: A permanent bronze statue of Creighton's mascot located at the entrance of the soccer stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Billy Bluejay statue is a permanent fixture in front of Morrison Stadium and is a popular spot for students to visit.
cards.source_title: The evolution of the Billy Bluejay mascot costume - Alumni and Friends
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors and accessible 24/7 for photos and visits.

cards.title: Create at the Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Tech Tuesday free projects
cards.notes: Join 'Tech Tuesday' for free guided projects using 3D printers and laser cutters. Training and design assistance are always free for students.
cards.short_summary: A creative technology workspace in the library offering tools for design and fabrication.
cards.evidence_claim: Tech Tuesday projects at the Makerspace provide free materials and instruction for students.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m.-4 p.m. for student use.

cards.title: Attend Taizé Prayer
cards.subtitle: Meditative evening prayer with music
cards.notes: Experience a peaceful evening of candlelit music and silence. These ecumenical services are held quarterly and are open to everyone.
cards.short_summary: A meditative Christian prayer service featuring repetitive songs and silence in a candlelit setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Prayer in the Style of Taizé is held at St. John's Church and is free and open to the Creighton and Omaha communities.
cards.access_notes: Held once per academic quarter at 7:00 p.m. on select Thursdays.

cards.title: Work Out at the KFC
cards.subtitle: Free gym access for students
cards.notes: Use the weight room, cardio equipment, or indoor track for free with your student ID. You can also check out basketballs and other gear at no cost.
cards.short_summary: The main campus recreation facility offering fitness equipment and sports courts.
cards.evidence_claim: All students can use the Kiewit Fitness Center (KFC) at no charge with a valid ID.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 6 a.m.-11 p.m. with reduced hours on weekends.

cards.title: Study in the Harper Center
cards.subtitle: Modern lounges and huddle rooms
cards.notes: Find a spot in the multi-level lounges or reserve a huddle room for group work. The building offers 24-hour card access for students.
cards.short_summary: A major campus building housing the business school and various student services with ample study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harper Center features study lounges and huddle rooms available for student use.
cards.source_title: Mike and Josie Harper Center - Creighton University
cards.access_notes: Building is open to the public until 11 p.m.; students have 24-hour card access.

cards.title: Join Birdcage Rewards
cards.subtitle: Free student rewards program
cards.notes: Download the app to earn points just for attending Creighton athletic events. Points can be redeemed for free prizes and exclusive gear.
cards.short_summary: A student-only program that rewards attendance at campus sporting events with points for prizes.
cards.evidence_claim: Birdcage Rewards is an exclusive free student reward app for Creighton University students.
cards.access_notes: Available to all current Creighton students via mobile app.

cards.title: Walk the One-Mile Mall
cards.subtitle: Brick pathway connecting campus
cards.notes: Stroll along the iconic brick pathway that stretches a full mile across campus. It's the best way to see the university's landmarks for free.
cards.short_summary: A mile-long brick pedestrian pathway that serves as the main artery of the Creighton campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mall is a mile-long brick pathway connecting the east and west ends of campus, open for public walking.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian path accessible 24/7.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From silent library floors to bustling student centers, Creighton University offers a variety of environments for focused academic work and collaborative projects.

cards.title: The Silent Zone
cards.subtitle: Reinert-Alumni Memorial Library
cards.notes: Head to the bottom level for absolute silence. This floor strictly prohibits snacks and talking, making it ideal for high-stakes exam preparation.
cards.short_summary: A strictly silent study floor in the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The bottom level of the Reinert-Alumni Memorial Library is designated as dead quiet with no snacks or talking allowed.
cards.source_title: Brenda Bluejay: Best Study Spots - Creightonian
cards.access_notes: Open to students with ID; hours vary by semester but typically open at 8am on weekdays.

cards.title: Collaborative Huddle Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mike and Josie Harper Center
cards.notes: Utilize these glass-walled rooms for group projects or speech practice. They offer a professional environment within the Heider College of Business.
cards.short_summary: Private group study rooms located in the Harper Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mike and Josie Harper Center features huddle rooms and lounge spaces for student studying.
cards.source_title: Mike and Josie Harper Center - Creighton University
cards.access_notes: Available for student use; huddle rooms are highly sought after and may require early arrival.

cards.title: The MOO Lounge
cards.subtitle: Hixson-Lied Science Building
cards.notes: Find a spot in this popular lounge within the science hub. It provides a bright, central location for science students to connect between labs.
cards.short_summary: A popular student lounge in the Hixson-Lied Science Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hixson-Lied Science Building houses the popular Mutual of Omaha (MOO) Lounge for students.
cards.access_notes: Located in the science building; accessible during building operating hours.

cards.title: Fireplace Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Skutt Student Center
cards.notes: Grab a coffee from the adjacent Starbucks and settle in by the central fireplace for a cozy, social study atmosphere in the campus 'living room'.
cards.short_summary: A cozy study area near the fireplace in the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Skutt Student Center features a cozy central fireplace area used for study sessions.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; central location often has background noise from the dining area.

cards.title: The Outdoor Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: Behind St. John's Church
cards.notes: Study amidst flowers and sculptures in this peaceful outdoor space. It is perfect for reading when you need a break from indoor classrooms.
cards.short_summary: A scenic outdoor garden area used for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jesuit Gardens are described as a quiet and peaceful place for students to study surrounded by nature.
cards.source_title: Brenda Bluejay: Best Study Spots - Creightonian
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; best during daylight hours and fair weather.

cards.title: Legal Research Center
cards.subtitle: Ahmanson Law Center
cards.notes: Access this quiet space for serious research. While primarily for law students, it serves the entire university community seeking a scholarly environment.
cards.short_summary: The primary legal research and study space on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Klutznick Law Library offers quiet space for study and research for the entire Creighton population.
cards.access_notes: Building access with Creighton ID required after 7pm and on weekends.

cards.title: The Collaborative Level
cards.subtitle: Reinert-Alumni Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use the large, comfortable booths on the top floor for group discussions. This level allows for quiet conversation and collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: The top floor of the main library, designated for quiet discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: The top level of the Reinert-Alumni Library allows for quiet discussion and features large booths for groups.
cards.source_title: Brenda Bluejay: Best Study Spots - Creightonian
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; booths are popular for small groups.

cards.title: Modern Health Science Hub
cards.subtitle: Werner Center
cards.notes: Study in this new facility featuring large windows and open spaces designed for interprofessional education and natural light.
cards.short_summary: A new health sciences building with modern, light-filled study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The CL and Rachel Werner Center features open spaces and large windows to invite natural light for students.
cards.source_title: Photo gallery: A tour of Creighton's new health sciences building
cards.access_notes: Primarily serves health sciences students but open to the campus community.

cards.title: The KFC Spine
cards.subtitle: Kiewit Fitness Center
cards.notes: Utilize the study areas along the 'spine' of the fitness center. It's a convenient spot for students who want to transition quickly between exercise and academics.
cards.short_summary: Study spaces located within the Kiewit Fitness Center corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'KFC Spine' is identified as a study area on campus for students.
cards.source_title: Creighton University: Best Places To Study For Finals
cards.access_notes: Accessible during KFC operating hours; can be noisy due to proximity to gym courts.

cards.title: Reservable Group Rooms
cards.subtitle: Reinert-Alumni Memorial Library
cards.notes: Book these rooms online for up to two hours. They come equipped with whiteboards and monitors for collaborative sessions.
cards.short_summary: Online-reservable study rooms for individuals or small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can reserve study rooms online at the Reinert-Alumni Library for up to two hours.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via the library website; limited to 2-hour blocks.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the streets and districts immediately surrounding Creighton University, from the historic Old Market to the rising Builder's District.

cards.title: The Builder's District
cards.subtitle: Cuming Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk east on Cuming Street to reach this new urban village featuring retail, dining, and the Kiewit Corporation headquarters.
cards.short_summary: A 10-block mixed-use urban village adjacent to Creighton's east campus featuring modern retail and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Builder's District is a 10-block urban village anchored by Kiewit Corporation's headquarters, connecting directly to Creighton's east campus.
cards.source_title: Creighton's new $650 million neighbor brings the city and University closer together than ever
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; pedestrian-friendly corridor connects to campus via 17th Street.

cards.title: Blackstone District
cards.subtitle: Farnam Street Corridor
cards.notes: Take the ORBT bus west on Dodge to Farnam Street for local favorites like Mula and Cheeseburgers.
cards.short_summary: A revitalized historic district along Farnam Street known for its diverse dining scene and student-friendly eateries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blackstone District is a revitalized historic district extending from 36th to 42nd Street along Farnam Street, popular with Creighton students.
cards.source_title: 11 student-friendly Omaha restaurants you can get to with your JayPass
cards.access_notes: Easily accessible via the Metro ORBT bus system using a student JayPass.

cards.title: The Old Market
cards.subtitle: Howard and Harney Streets
cards.notes: Visit this historic warehouse district for brick-lined streets, eclectic shops, and student staples like Ted & Wally's Ice Cream.
cards.short_summary: Omaha's premier historic district featuring cobblestone streets and a high concentration of restaurants and galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old Market is a historic warehouse district with brick streets and over 45 restaurants, located about a mile south of campus.
cards.access_notes: Public historic district; most shops and restaurants are open daily.

cards.title: Midtown Crossing
cards.subtitle: 33rd and Dodge Streets
cards.notes: Stop here for boba at Thirst Tea Café or wood-fired pizza at Smokin' Oak, just five minutes from campus.
cards.short_summary: A modern mixed-use development offering dining, entertainment, and green space at Turner Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Midtown Crossing is a vibrant development five minutes from campus featuring coffee shops, vegan comfort food, and boba.
cards.access_notes: Features Turner Park, which hosts free community events like Jazz on the Green.

cards.title: The Capitol District
cards.subtitle: 10th and Capitol Avenue
cards.notes: Head to this downtown plaza for outdoor events and dining near the CHI Health Center.
cards.short_summary: A modern entertainment district in downtown Omaha centered around a large outdoor plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: The Capitol District is an urban hub for restaurants and nightlife located just steps from the CHI Health Center.
cards.access_notes: The central plaza is a public space; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: North 24th Street
cards.subtitle: 24th and Lake Streets
cards.notes: Explore the historic heart of North Omaha, home to the Fair Deal Village MarketPlace and local vegan spot Ital Vital Living.
cards.short_summary: A historic cultural corridor in North Omaha featuring local businesses and community markets.
cards.evidence_claim: Route 24 connects Creighton to local flavor in North Omaha, including plant-based café Ital Vital Living at 24th and Grant.
cards.source_title: 11 student-friendly Omaha restaurants you can get to with your JayPass
cards.access_notes: Accessible via Metro Route 24 from 24th and Dodge.

cards.title: Gene Leahy Mall
cards.subtitle: Douglas Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk down Douglas Street to this massive downtown park for the slides, hammocks, and performance pavilions.
cards.short_summary: A newly revitalized 57-acre park system linking downtown Omaha to the Missouri River.
cards.evidence_claim: Gene Leahy Mall at The RiverFront is a revitalized downtown green space with lawns and playgrounds, linking the Old Market to the riverfront.
cards.source_title: Creighton University Guide: Where to Eat, Drink & Stay in Omaha (2026)
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.

cards.title: Civic Square
cards.subtitle: 18th and Capitol Avenue
cards.notes: Check out this developing 9-acre site between campus and downtown, planned to include a grocery store and healthcare services.
cards.short_summary: A modern mixed-use development on the site of the former Civic Auditorium, bridging campus and the city center.
cards.evidence_claim: Civic Square is a 9-acre mixed-use development positioned between Downtown Omaha and Creighton University.
cards.access_notes: Currently under development; pedestrian access available along the perimeter.

cards.title: South 24th Street
cards.subtitle: South Omaha Business District
cards.notes: Ride the bus south to find authentic Mexican cuisine at Birrieria El Chalan and explore the culturally diverse shops.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant, culturally rich business district in South Omaha known for its dining and bilingual services.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Omaha Business District on South 24th Street is a destination for culturally diverse dining and shopping.
cards.source_title: South Omaha Business District | South 24th Street
cards.access_notes: Accessible via Metro Route 24; most businesses are open during standard retail hours.

cards.title: Millwork Commons
cards.subtitle: 13th and Nicholas Streets
cards.notes: Walk north of the Builder's District to find this tech and arts hub featuring Archetype Coffee and community workspaces.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative neighborhood north of downtown Omaha designed for innovators, artists, and students.
cards.evidence_claim: Millwork Commons is an emerging district located north of the Builder's District and downtown proper.
cards.source_title: 1501 Mike Fahey Building in the Builders District - Omaha Exploration
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible neighborhood; features outdoor plazas and indoor community spaces.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique Jesuit heritage and student-led rituals that define the Bluejay experience at Creighton University.

cards.title: Christmas at Creighton
cards.subtitle: The Annual Lighting Ceremony
cards.notes: Gather at St. John's Church for the 'flipping of the switch' to illuminate the campus with thousands of blue lights and a festive Nativity scene.
cards.short_summary: A 40-year-old tradition where the campus is illuminated with blue lights to mark the start of the holiday season.
cards.evidence_claim: The holiday season kicks off with the highly anticipated 'flipping of the switch' at St. John's Church, lighting up campus with thousands of bulbs and blue glow.
cards.source_title: Photos: Christmas at Creighton through the years
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; typically held in early December.

cards.title: Rubbing Billy's Beak
cards.subtitle: A Ritual for Good Luck
cards.notes: Visit the bronze Billy Bluejay statue near Morrison Stadium to rub his beak for good luck before exams or major athletic events.
cards.short_summary: Students rub the beak of the 6-foot-tall bronze mascot statue for luck.
cards.evidence_claim: The Billy Bluejay statue, a 6-foot-tall painted bronze work from 2004, serves as a focal point for campus spirit and tradition.
cards.source_title: Billy Bluejay | Bluejay Statue at Placzek Studios
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors in front of Morrison Stadium; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: A Jesuit Academic Opening
cards.notes: Participate in this centuries-old Jesuit tradition where the community gathers to seek guidance for the upcoming academic year.
cards.short_summary: A traditional Jesuit liturgy held at the start of the academic year to seek divine guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: A tradition among Jesuit academic institutions dating to 1548 in which the community gathers to thank God and seek guidance for the coming year.
cards.source_title: Show Your Creighton Spirit | Alumni and Friends
cards.access_notes: Held annually during the first weeks of the fall semester.

cards.title: The JayWalk
cards.subtitle: Annual Charity Run/Walk
cards.notes: Join the Creighton Students Union for a mile-long race across campus starting at St. John's Fountain to raise funds for the Jesuit Academy.
cards.short_summary: An annual run/walk event that brings the community together to support local Jesuit education.
cards.evidence_claim: The 23rd Annual Jaywalk brought Bluejays together to run, walk and celebrate tradition, supporting the Jesuit Academy in Omaha.
cards.access_notes: Registration required for participants; typically held in the fall.

cards.title: Welcome Week Lip Sync
cards.subtitle: High-Energy Performance Competition
cards.notes: Watch student groups compete in elaborate choreographed lip-sync routines during Welcome Week to win the title of best performance.
cards.short_summary: A popular Welcome Week competition featuring themed lip-sync performances by student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Fraternities, sororities and RSP groups compete in the annual Lip Sync contest to win the title of best Lip Sync.
cards.access_notes: Held annually during Welcome Week in August.

cards.title: Founders Week
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the Creighton Legacy
cards.notes: Attend the annual convocation to honor the Creighton family's vision and recognize outstanding community members with awards.
cards.short_summary: A week of events in early February dedicated to the university's history and its founding family.
cards.evidence_claim: During Founders Week, we recognize and reflect on our journey as a University throughout our more than 145-year history.
cards.access_notes: Events are held across campus; convocation is a highlight.

cards.title: Baccalaureate Mass
cards.subtitle: A Spiritual Send-off
cards.notes: Join graduating seniors and their families for a final communal liturgy before the formal commencement ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A significant pre-graduation Mass that celebrates and blesses the departing senior class.
cards.evidence_claim: The Baccalaureate Mass is held during Commencement weekend to celebrate, bless, and send forth Creighton University's graduating class.
cards.access_notes: Tickets are not required for entry; open to graduates and guests.

cards.title: The Eternal Flame
cards.subtitle: Heart of the Campus Mall
cards.notes: Visit the iconic fountain topped with the Eternal Flame sculpture, a gift from local labor unions that serves as a central campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: A landmark fountain and sculpture that symbolizes the enduring spirit of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: The Eternal Flame sculpture has stood on the St. John's Fountain for nearly 30 years as one of the most iconic spots at Creighton.
cards.source_title: The odd history of the Fountain, the Mall and the nude sculpture
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Lilac Giving Cords
cards.subtitle: Philanthropy at Graduation
cards.notes: Seniors who contribute to the class gift receive a lilac cord to wear during commencement, continuing a tradition of student philanthropy.
cards.short_summary: A tradition where graduating seniors wear lilac cords to signify their contribution to the university's future.
cards.evidence_claim: Seniors who make a gift of $10 or more to any area of campus will receive a lilac giving cord to wear at graduation.
cards.source_title: Senior Class Giving - Alumni and Friends
cards.access_notes: Cords are distributed to participating seniors prior to graduation.

cards.title: Walking the Pathway
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week Procession
cards.notes: New students walk the campus pathway during Welcome Week, symbolically entering the Creighton community as they begin their journey.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic walk taken by new students to mark their official entry into the university.
cards.evidence_claim: New students moved into their residence halls, walked the Pathway, and took part in campus traditions during Welcome Week.
cards.source_title: Creighton Welcome Week 2024: Class of 2028 Begins Their Bluejay Journey
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in mid-August during freshman orientation.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Creighton University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide for new Bluejays to navigate their first weekend on campus, from move-in traditions to finding your favorite study and social spots.

cards.title: Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned residence hall during your scheduled timeslot to begin the move-in process and meet your new floor mates.
cards.short_summary: The official start of your Creighton journey begins with moving into your campus home.
cards.evidence_claim: Fall 2026 Move-In Weekend will take place August 14-15, 2026, with specific timeslots assigned to first-year students.
cards.access_notes: Check your Creighton email for your specific move-in timeslot and building location.

cards.title: President's Welcome Picnic
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Social
cards.notes: Join the university president and fellow new students for a community meal to celebrate the start of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A traditional outdoor picnic hosted by the University President for new students and families.
cards.evidence_claim: The President's Welcome Picnic is listed as a sample event for Welcome Week, typically occurring during the move-in period.
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and their families during Welcome Week.

cards.title: Photo with Billy
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Landmark
cards.notes: Stop by the bronze statue of Billy Bluejay outside Morrison Stadium for a classic first-weekend photo op.
cards.short_summary: An iconic bronze statue of the university mascot located at the entrance of the soccer stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The bronze statue of Billy Bluejay is located outside the Michael G. Morrison, S.J. Stadium on the Creighton campus.
cards.source_title: The evolution of the Billy Bluejay mascot costume - Alumni and Friends
cards.access_notes: Outdoor statue accessible 24/7 for photos.

cards.title: Explore Skutt Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Hub
cards.notes: Visit the student union to find the bookstore, dining options, and student organization offices.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, featuring dining, meeting spaces, and the university bookstore.
cards.evidence_claim: The Skutt Student Center is the most popular student commons and houses the Student Leadership and Involvement Center.
cards.access_notes: Standard building hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. on weekdays; check for weekend Welcome Week hours.

cards.title: Lunch at Brandeis
cards.subtitle: Saturday Midday Meal
cards.notes: Grab a meal at the main campus dining hall, which is the only one typically open for full service on weekends.
cards.short_summary: The primary all-you-care-to-eat resident dining facility on the Creighton campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Brandeis Dining Hall is an all-you-care-to-eat facility and is the only dining hall open on the weekends.
cards.access_notes: Requires a student meal swipe or payment via cash/card.

cards.title: Sundaes on Saturday
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Treat
cards.notes: Enjoy a free ice cream sundae while mingling with other new students during this Welcome Week tradition.
cards.short_summary: A social event featuring ice cream sundaes for new students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: Sundaes on Saturday is listed as a recurring Welcome Week event for new students and families.
cards.access_notes: Check the Welcome Week schedule for the specific campus location each year.

cards.title: Workout at the KFC
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Activity
cards.notes: Check out the renovated fitness center for a quick workout, a game of basketball, or to visit the esports suite.
cards.short_summary: The main campus recreation facility, featuring weight rooms, courts, and an indoor track.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kiewit Fitness Center (KFC) is the main recreation center on campus and includes weight rooms, courts, and an esports suite.
cards.access_notes: Free for students with a valid Creighton ID. Saturday hours are typically 9 a.m. to 10 p.m.

cards.title: Welcome Week Mass
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Service
cards.notes: Attend the Welcome Week Mass at the historic campus church to experience a cornerstone of Creighton's Jesuit identity.
cards.short_summary: A special liturgy held at St. John's Church to welcome the new academic community.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Week Mass is a featured event during the orientation period at St. John's Church on campus.
cards.access_notes: Open to all; check the parish website for specific Sunday Mass times.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Prep
cards.notes: Visit the library to scope out quiet study areas and check out the Makerspace before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: The main academic library at Creighton, offering research resources and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Reinert-Alumni Memorial Library is the center of academic life and requires a Creighton ID for access after 7 p.m. and all day on weekends.
cards.access_notes: Creighton ID required for weekend entry.

cards.title: Relax at Deglman Square
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Wind-down
cards.notes: Spend some time in this central outdoor plaza, a popular spot for students to gather and relax between events.
cards.short_summary: A central campus plaza used for social interaction and various student activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Deglman Square is a recognized campus location often used for student gatherings and events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space accessible 24/7.
